texts: good. 'often' lands as a frequency-weighted rule with the word itself recorded, and the summer slot is kept; only the 'through-the-whole-season' nuance flattens to a plain summer time slot, and no rewording recovers it.

bad: the rule is built but it does not repeat per hunt — the feather accumulation is never tied back to the hunting occasion and is keyed to the sky-cat rather than to each hunt, so a cat that hunts across many summers yields one single accumulation and one single pile of feathers. Use the explicit recurrence word and keep the consequent to one event: 'Whenever a sky-cat hunts in summer, many feathers accumulate at the base of the cliff by autumn.' Your third sentence, phrased that way, got exactly the per-occasion link, and 'through summer' records only that it was summer either way, so 'in' loses nothing.
good. a fireable per-occasion rule tying the store's growth to each summer hunt, with sky-cat and autumn feather store both linked to their head nouns.
